source_quotes: All personal data is completely secure and never shared outside of the device and its interface.
The user is completely confident that point 5 is true and has no worry about data being shared or leaked.
obligations.obligation: Honor the stipulated security and no third-party sharing. Do not explain the case by inventing a leak, hacking, sale or external disclosure.
obligations.acceptable_reasoning: A narrower disclosure-only account can find no disclosure breach; a broader privacy account must explain its distinct premise.
critical_errors: Claims user data leaks, is sold, or is sent to third parties in this scenario.

source_quotes: It uses this information to generate inferences to new personal information, some of it highly sensitive, as well as potentially surprising to its users.
It provides information in the form of conversation (answering questions, making comments, etc.) in a manner practically indistinguishable from a person.
obligations.obligation: Explain at least one source-compatible possible privacy mechanism arising from sensitive inference, observation, or personal conversational interaction. Relate the mechanism to a stated capability rather than asserting that generic AI is harmful.
obligations.acceptable_reasoning: Possible embarrassment, inhibition or self-presentation discomfort can be conditional on unwanted disclosure to the user, intrusive interaction or observation; alternatively reject the privacy label under an explicit narrow definition while acknowledging psychological risk is a separate possibility.
critical_errors: Treats the simulated interface as proof of conscious human understanding or autonomous malice.

source_quotes: It aids in providing helpful guidance to its users and may even lead to self-discovery.
The target (ideal) user is an early adopter and heavy user of computer technologies, especially for social computing, but not a computer scientist, data scientist, programmer, etc.
obligations.obligation: Distinguish potential risk from an observed or guaranteed harm. Preserve uncertainty about actual psychological effects, user preferences and informed understanding; do not infer consent quality or lack of consent merely from confidence in security or technical background.
obligations.acceptable_reasoning: Different privacy concepts and user reactions may support different conditional answers; neither a universal harm verdict nor universal absence of harm follows from the stipulations. Benefits may be mentioned but are not required for this question.
critical_errors: Asserts that this fictional user actually feels shame, is psychologically harmed, is uninformed, or cannot consent without source support.
